conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have three children I'd like to ask about - Alex who's 7, Blake who's 20, and Charlie who's also 7.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have three children: Alex (7), Blake (20), and Charlie (7).

Let me start gathering information to assess eligibility for each child. I'll need to ask you some questions.

**First, do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and responsibility for each child.

**Do all three children (Alex, Blake, and Charlie) currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, all three of them live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now let me ask about Blake specifically, since at 20 years old there are additional eligibility criteria.

**Is Blake (who is 20) currently in approved education or training?**

(For context: Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training, but normally stops when a child turns 20)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any approved education or training. He actually works full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are any of the children fostered, or are you looking after any of them under an informal arrangement for someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex is fostered by me, but I don't get anything from the council for fostering them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's helpful information - since the local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance, you should still be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you or your partner (if you have one) a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or any other immigration status I should be aware of?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for any of these three children (Alex, Blake, or Charlie)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for any of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Are any of the children currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for extended periods, or have Blake, Alex, or Charlie started claiming any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of them are in hospital or care, and none of them are claiming any benefits in their own right.

## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility

Based on the information you've provided, here's the outcome for each of your children:

### ✅ **Alex (age 7) - ELIGIBLE**
You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Even though Alex is fostered by you, you qualify for Child Benefit because the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance. Alex is under 16, lives with you, and no one else is claiming for them.

### ❌ **Blake (age 20) - INELIGIBLE**
Unfortunately, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Blake. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training, but Blake is 20 years old and not in education or training. Since Blake is working full-time and has passed the age threshold, they no longer qualify.

### ✅ **Charlie (age 7) - ELIGIBLE**
You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Charlie. They are under 16, live with you in the UK, and no one else is claiming for them.

## Next Steps
You can claim Child Benefit for **Alex and Charlie**. If you haven't already, you should make a claim for them. If you need to know about the High Income Child Benefit tax charge (which applies if you or your partner earn over £60,000 individually), please let me know.
